correctness.rationale: The block Laplacian (n−1+L_H,−R;−Rᵀ,L_2+2) is established by exact move counting. The intertwining L_2 Rᵀ=RᵀL_H, Gram RRᵀ=(n−2)I+J, and explicit L_2 spectrum of m isolates plus q squares yield a complete invariant-space splitting. The paired blocks have eigenvalues (0,n+1), (1,n), (3,n+2), while ker R contributes (2,4,6) with dimensions (q,m(m−2),q); all dimensions and boundary coincidences agree. Kirchhoff produces the exact spanning-tree product. Two independent constructed code checkers passed characteristic polynomials m=2..8, modular nullities/cofactors m=2..9, and exact cofactors m=2..4.

originality.rationale: Full-length primary research texts on symmetric squares, token graph basics and Laplacian lifting were examined, and targeted full-text searches identified no all-eigenvalue formula for the 2-token friendship graph. The established general intertwining relation accounts for the inherited eigenvalues, not the remaining dimensions. The new derivation explicitly resolves all remaining dimensions and the tree product. Search absence is not proof of absolute novelty; unindexed or differently named prior work is a residual risk.

value.rationale: This computes the complete spectral arithmetic and exact tree complexity for a canonical infinite family of nonregular two-particle exclusion graphs. It explains integral eigenvalues and fixed spectral gap 1 using a structural decomposition, not an ad hoc small census. The residual square/isolate geometry matters naturally to understanding hard-core particle motion; exact spectrum and spanning-tree count can serve as benchmarks for reconfiguration networks and related stochastic processes.
